title: 12 Transformations of functions: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 12 Transformations of functions: Visual Guide

1. Vertex Form Again | the already-taught vertex form y = a(x-h)^2 + k and the circle equation beside the general y = f(x-h) + k, with h and k sliders, a swappable starting curve (x^2, |x|, x^3) and a table showing the same heights landing at new inputs | vertex form and the circle equation were one rule written twice with the curve baked in, so replacing the curve by a nameless f keeps every conclusion: k sits outside f and moves the graph vertically, h sits inside f and moves it horizontally, and neither changes the shape

2. Inside Or Outside | the same number c written outside f as f(x) + c and inside f as f(x - c), toggled side by side with a c slider, the plotted vertex, a values table and preset buttons for f(x)+3, f(x)-3, f(x-2) and f(x+2) | outside f the sign is honest, so y = f(x) + 3 is a shift upward by 3 units; inside f it runs backwards, so y = (x-2)^2 sits 2 to the RIGHT of y = x^2 - and the reliable move is never to memorise a direction but to set the inside expression equal to zero and solve

3. Two Mirrors | the outside mirror y = -f(x) and the inside mirror y = f(-x) switched on independently over x^2, x^3 and (x-1)^2, with a table of f(x), -f(x) and f(-x) and a verdict on whether the mirrored copy landed back on f | -f(x) negates the output and flips across the x-axis while f(-x) negates the input and flips across the y-axis, so with f(x) = x^2 they are -x^2 and (-x)^2 = x^2, two different functions - and the case where a mirror changes nothing at all is what visual 5 names

4. Stretch The Outputs | a in g(x) = a f(x) dragged from -3 to 4 over f(x) = x + 1, with the graph, the distributed rule 4(x+1) = 4x+4 against the trap 4x+1, one sampled value scaled, the pinned x-intercept and presets for 4f(x), 3f(x), (1/2)f(x) and -2f(x) | a multiplier outside f multiplies every output, so 3f(x) is a vertical stretch by a factor of 3, (1/2)f(x) halves each output value, a negative a reflects over the x-axis and then stretches by |a|, and the multiplier hits the whole rule - never just its first term

5. Fold Or Spin | eight functions (x^2, x^3, x^4, x, x^5+x, x^2+1, x^2+x, |x|) folded across the y-axis as f(-x) and spun 180 degrees about the origin as -f(-x), with a live even/odd/neither verdict and a draggable test value showing both conditions evaluated | even means f(-x) = f(x) with y-axis symmetry and odd means f(-x) = -f(x) with origin symmetry, the parity of a power follows the parity of its exponent, oddness turns f(3) = -2 into f(-3) = 2 with no further work, and because both conditions are claimed for EVERY x one counterexample settles it - most functions are neither
